target_question: Does the contemporaneous experiment-team publication or a mission/range report identify the actual launch date of Aerobee USAF 26 / Aeromed 3 carrying Patricia, Mike, Mildred and Albert as 1952-05-21 or 1952-05-22?

highest_priority_identified_source.title: Animal studies of the subgravity state during rocket flight
highest_priority_identified_source.why_high_priority: The article was published months after the final Aerobee animal flight by the experiment team itself and is therefore a near-contemporaneous source likely to contain experiment chronology, vehicle or flight details.
highest_priority_identified_source.fail_closed_rule: Do not infer a launch date from the article title/citation alone.

supporting_official_history_source.source: This New Ocean: A History of Project Mercury / NASA history lineage
supporting_official_history_source.relevant_citation: The NASA history cites Henry et al. for the Holloman V-2/Aerobee animal experiments and describes the final Aerobee shot as occurring in May 1952, but the accessible passage does not adjudicate day 21 versus 22.

sources_supporting_1952_05_21: Holloman AFB official chronology: the five V-2 plus three Aerobee series ran through 21 May 1952, with survival of two monkeys and two mice in the final flights.
National Museum of the U.S. Air Force photo metadata: Aerobee launch team at Holloman AFB dated 21 May 1952; supporting timing evidence, not unique payload identity.
Frozen GCAT independent derivative: Aerobee RTV-A-1 / USAF 26 / Aeromed 3 / HADC / Biology at 1952-05-21 15:15 UTC.
sources_supporting_1952_05_22: National Museum of the U.S. Air Force Aerobee public fact sheet directly names Patricia and Mike and dates the flight to 22 May 1952.
NASA modern public animal-space history lineage used by the historical JANUS parent manifest gives 22 May 1952.
current_source_balance.unresolved_reason: The 21-May lineage has stronger launch-chronology structure, while the 22-May lineage has direct payload-name public-history wording. A contemporaneous flight, range, telemetry, laboratory or experiment-team source is still required for a clean resolution.

acceptable_resolution_sources: Open full text or scan of Henry, Ballinger, Maher and Simons (1952), especially experiment chronology/table material.
Contemporaneous Holloman/HADC/USAF 26 launch log or range record.
Aero-Medical Laboratory / WADC Physiology of Rocket Flight project report identifying USAF 26 / Aeromed 3.
Contemporaneous telemetry, recovery, mission or experiment report with launch date and vehicle identity.
not_acceptable_for_resolution: Changing the date solely to make GCAT pass the old 6/6 gate.
Using Blue Book or POSS outcomes to choose between 21 and 22 May.
Treating repeated modern secondary copies as independent launch-date evidence.
Inferring a date from a citation when the underlying text has not been read.
